movie.title: Motor City
movie.overview: In 1970s Detroit, John Miller falls for a local gangster's girl and lands in prison for a crime he didn't commit. With his life ruined, Miller plots revenge against the man who took his girl away.

reviews.author: The Fixate & Binge Podcast, w/ Joe Curdy
reviews.content:
Alfred Hitchcock once declared that filmmakers "should only resort to dialogue when it is completely impossible to tell the story visually" and famously critiqued dialogue-heavy films as merely "photographs of people talking."

However one approaches director Potsy Ponciroli's **MOTOR CITY**, one thing becomes immediately clear: this is a visual story that throws out the rulebook of more traditional action films. 

With nearly zero dialogue -- co-star Ben MacKenzie's character never utters a single word -- and an enviable 1970s soundtrack -- Ponciroli picks up Hitchcock's gauntlet and delivers a crowd-pleasing revenge actioner with one of the most talented casts working in Hollywood today.

Brick shithouse Alan Ritchson fills the screen as John Miller with his hulking, brooding presence, carrying nuance like a kettlebell in scene after gloriously action-packed scene from beginning to end. His love interest -- Sophia (played by Shailene Woodley) oozes thoroughly believable onscreen chemistry with Ritchson. Their happy, blue-collar life is suddenly torn apart with a conspiracy to rival Alexander Dumas's ***The Count of Monte Cristo***.

With telling flashbacks and a **SERPICO**-esque glimpse at police corruption in 1970s Detroit, what happens next will slake the thirst of any action fan, as Ponciroli's film rides hell for leather in a relentless and brutal sequence of revenge.

Co-starring Ben Foster, Pablo Schreiber and Lionel Boyce, and a cameo by Detroit's own Jack White (who serves as one of the 28 executive producers) -- **MOTOR CITY** confirms what most action films dare to risk: dialogue is optional when a filmmaker understands how to tell a story visually.

**MOTOR CITY** is sure to divide critics -- and is likely doomed at the box office for the misfortune of being stuck between a rock and a hard place (released between **THE ODYSSEY** and **SPIDER-MAN: BRAND NEW DAY**) -- yet one hopes it will build on a solid word-of-mouth success and excel once it moves to streaming.

In a "less is more" approach to this revenge actioner -- which is precisely what made George Miller's **MAD MAX: FURY ROAD** and both of Jalmari Helander's much-loved Finnish **SISU** films so great -- **MOTOR CITY** gives audiences a visual feast without holding their hands. 

The principal cast offer standout performances -- especially in one memorable, entirely wordless seductive sequence between Woodley and Foster in a late-night coffee shop rendezvous. This is arguably Woodley's best work. Equally impressive, Ritchson cements himself as one of the most watchable actors in Hollywood today.

aiEnrichment.summary_one_sentence: Framed and imprisoned by a ruthless gangster in 1970s Detroit, John Miller embarks on a relentless quest for revenge to reclaim his life and the woman he loves.
aiEnrichment.summary_short: Set against the gritty backdrop of 1970s Detroit, honest mechanic John Miller's life is shattered when he falls in love with a local gangster's girl. Framed for a crime he didn't commit, he is torn away from everything he knows and sent to prison. Driven by betrayal and loss, Miller bides his time behind bars to plot a methodical payback. Upon his release, he launches a high-stakes campaign against the underworld kingpin who destroyed his future.
aiEnrichment.summary_long: In the vibrant yet gritty atmosphere of 1970s Detroit, John Miller leads a simple life until he falls deeply in love with a woman connected to a powerful local gangster. Enraged by the betrayal, the criminal kingpin orchestrates a setup that frames Miller for a major crime he did not commit. Stripped of his freedom and separated from the love of his life, Miller is sentenced to hard time in prison. Behind bars, the brutal reality of incarceration tempers his despair into cold, calculating rage. He focuses his mind on a single goal: exacting vengeance upon the man who ruined his life and stole his passion. Over years of confinement, Miller studies his enemies, learns to survive, and meticulously maps out his retribution. When he finally steps back onto the streets of Detroit, he is no longer the innocent man who was sent away. Armed with unwavering resolve, he systematically unravels the gangster's empire, tracking down every associate involved in his downfall. As the violent confrontation reaches its climax, Miller risks everything in a desperate bid for justice and redemption.
aiEnrichment.synopsis: Motor City is a gritty 1970s period action-thriller centered on John Miller, an ordinary man whose world collapses after he pursues a romance with a dangerous Detroit gangster's girlfriend. retaliating against the perceived slight, the crime lord uses his influence to frame Miller, resulting in a harsh prison sentence. Stripped of his freedom and forced to endure years behind bars, Miller transforms his grief into an unyielding determination for revenge. The film delves into themes of love, injustice, and relentless retribution as Miller navigates the treacherous urban underworld to confront the powerful syndicate that took everything from him.

faq.answer: The film was directed by Potsy Ponciroli, known for directing Old Henry (2021) and Greedy People (2024).

faq.question: When and where is Motor City set?
